title: Global Food Companies Use Lawsuits to Block Health Rules
subtitle: New reports show how legal battles are delaying efforts to fight the obesity crisis worldwide.

summary.en: Major food companies are frequently using lawsuits to challenge government health policies. These actions often target rules like warning labels and taxes on unhealthy foods. According to The Guardian Health, these legal battles have caused significant delays in public health improvements. While many companies claim to support health, their legal actions suggest a different strategy. This ongoing issue continues to cost governments billions of dollars in legal and healthcare expenses.
summary.zh: 大型食品公司頻繁利用訴訟挑戰政府的健康政策。這些行動通常針對警示標籤與垃圾食物稅等規定。根據《衛報健康》報導，這些法律戰已導致公共衛生的改善出現嚴重延宕。儘管許多公司聲稱支持健康，但其法律行動卻顯示出截然不同的策略。此問題持續造成各國政府在法律與醫療支出上損失數十億美元。

paragraphs.en: A major investigation has revealed that some of the world’s largest food companies are actively working to stop governments from passing laws that promote healthier eating. These companies, which produce large amounts of ultra-processed food—items that have been heavily changed from their natural state and often contain added sugar, salt, and fats—are increasingly using the court system to challenge new health regulations. According to The Guardian Health, these actions are creating significant obstacles for countries trying to address the growing global obesity crisis.
paragraphs.zh: 一項重大調查揭露，全球部分大型食品公司正積極阻撓各國政府通過促進健康飲食的法案。這些生產大量「超加工食品」（即經過高度加工、脫離天然狀態，且通常添加糖、鹽與脂肪的食品）的企業，正日益利用司法體系來挑戰新的健康法規。根據《衛報健康》（The Guardian Health）報導，這些行為正為試圖解決全球日益嚴重肥胖危機的國家，製造了巨大的障礙。

paragraphs.en: Publicly, many of these large food corporations say they want to help people make better choices. They often claim to support policies that improve public health. However, a detailed investigation by The Guardian Health and several partners found that these same companies often take governments to court. Their goal is frequently to overturn, weaken, or delay rules such as front-of-pack warning labels, marketing restrictions, and taxes on junk food. These legal tactics have been observed in several countries, including the United States, the United Kingdom, Mexico, Colombia, and Brazil.
paragraphs.zh: 公開場合中，許多大型食品企業聲稱希望協助民眾做出更好的選擇，並經常表示支持改善公共衛生的政策。然而，《衛報健康》與數個合作夥伴進行的詳細調查發現，這些公司私下卻經常將政府告上法庭。其目的往往是為了推翻、削弱或延宕各項規定，例如包裝正面的警示標籤、行銷限制以及針對垃圾食物課稅等。這些法律手段已在包括美國、英國、墨西哥、哥倫比亞與巴西在內的多個國家出現。

paragraphs.en: Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus, the leader of the World Health Organization, has spoken out against these tactics. He noted that when companies prioritize profit over public health, they often try to create doubt and stop necessary regulations. The report highlights that from 2010 to 2025, there were 235 lawsuits filed against health policies related to ultra-processed foods. While governments won about three-quarters of the cases that have been decided, the process itself is very damaging. Even when companies lose, the legal battles can last for years, forcing officials to spend time and money on court cases instead of focusing on public health.
paragraphs.zh: 世界衛生組織（World Health Organization）秘書長譚德塞（Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus）公開反對這些策略。他指出，當企業將利潤置於公共健康之上時，往往會試圖製造疑慮並阻撓必要的法規。報告強調，從二〇一〇年至二〇二五年，針對超加工食品相關健康政策的訴訟案件高達兩百三十五起。儘管政府在已判決的案件中贏得了約四分之三的勝訴，但訴訟過程本身極具破壞力。即便企業敗訴，法律戰仍可能持續數年，迫使官員將時間與金錢耗費在法庭訴訟上，而非專注於公共衛生事務。

paragraphs.en: These delays have real-world consequences. The Guardian Health reports that these lawsuits have caused nearly 600 cumulative years of legal fighting. This creates what experts call a "regulatory chill," where other governments become afraid to pass similar health laws because they do not want to face expensive and long-lasting legal challenges. This fear can stop important protections from being put in place, which ultimately makes the obesity crisis worse. Obesity is a major driver of serious health problems, including heart disease, type 2 diabetes, and cancer. With nearly 1 billion people worldwide living with obesity, the impact of these delays is significant.
paragraphs.zh: 這些延宕具有現實層面的後果。《衛報健康》報導指出，這些訴訟累計造成了近六百年的法律攻防。這創造了專家所謂的「法規寒蟬效應」，即其他政府因擔心面臨昂貴且曠日費時的法律挑戰，而不敢通過類似的健康法案。這種恐懼可能導致重要的保護措施無法落實，最終加劇了肥胖危機。肥胖是心臟病、第二型糖尿病與癌症等嚴重健康問題的主要成因。全球目前有近十億人飽受肥胖之苦，這些延宕帶來的影響相當深遠。

paragraphs.en: Researchers from organizations like the University of Sydney and the University of São Paulo helped analyze the scale of this problem. They found that the legal pushback from the food industry is not just about winning individual cases. Instead, it appears to be a strategy to slow down the rollout of new laws and discourage other nations from trying to regulate the industry. The cost of these battles is high, not just in legal fees, but in the billions of dollars that countries must spend on healthcare for conditions linked to poor diets.
paragraphs.zh: 來自雪梨大學（University of Sydney）與聖保羅大學（University of São Paulo）等機構的研究人員協助分析了此問題的規模。他們發現，食品產業的法律反擊不僅是為了贏得個別案件，更似乎是一種策略，旨在拖慢新法的推行，並嚇阻其他國家嘗試監管該產業。這些法律戰的代價高昂，不僅在於法律費用，更在於各國必須為與不良飲食相關的疾病，投入數十億美元的醫療支出。

paragraphs.en: As the world continues to struggle with the health impacts of ultra-processed foods, the tension between government regulation and corporate interests remains high. While some companies continue to argue that they are part of the solution, the findings from The Guardian Health suggest that their legal actions are often working against the very health goals they claim to support. For now, governments face a difficult path as they try to protect their citizens while navigating a landscape of constant legal pressure from powerful food corporations.
paragraphs.zh: 隨著全球持續與超加工食品帶來的健康影響搏鬥，政府監管與企業利益之間的緊張關係依然高漲。儘管部分公司持續辯稱自己是解決方案的一部分，但《衛報健康》的調查結果顯示，他們的法律行動往往與其聲稱支持的健康目標背道而馳。目前，各國政府在試圖保護公民的同時，仍須在強大食品企業持續施加的法律壓力下，面對艱難的處境。

keyTerms.definitionEn: To formally question the legality or validity of a law or decision in court.
keyTerms.definitionZh: 在法律上質疑或挑戰某項法規的合法性。
keyTerms.noteZh: 常見作名詞（挑戰），這裡作動詞，指透過法律手段反對法規。文中：these companies, which produce large amounts of ultra-processed food—items that have been heavily changed from their natural state and often contain added sugar, salt, and fats—are increasingly using the court system to challenge new health regulations.

keyTerms.definitionEn: To officially decide that a legal decision or rule is wrong and change it.
keyTerms.noteZh: 常見作動詞（翻倒物體），這裡指法律上的撤銷或推翻。文中：Their goal is frequently to overturn, weaken, or delay rules such as front-of-pack warning labels, marketing restrictions, and taxes on junk food.

keyTerms.definitionEn: A factor that causes or influences the development of something.
keyTerms.definitionZh: 驅動因素、導致某事發生的主要原因。
keyTerms.noteZh: 常見作名詞（司機），這裡指導致某種情況發生的核心因素。文中：Obesity is a major driver of serious health problems, including heart disease, type 2 diabetes, and cancer.

keyTerms.definitionEn: A negative or opposing reaction to a plan or policy.
keyTerms.noteZh: 由動詞片語 push back 轉變而來的名詞，指來自對方的強烈反彈。文中：They found that the legal pushback from the food industry is not just about winning individual cases.

previousArticles.title: Big Food Companies Use Legal Battles to Block Health Rules
previousArticles.summaryEn: The World Health Organization reports that major food companies are suing governments to stop healthy eating policies. These companies often try to block warning labels and taxes on ultra-processed foods. Although many companies claim to support public health, they frequently use legal action to delay new rules. These lawsuits have caused years of delays and cost countries billions in legal and healthcare expenses. Experts warn that this behavior makes it harder for nations to protect their citizens from diet-related diseases.

quiz.question: According to the article, what is the primary outcome for governments when they win legal battles against food companies?

options.A: They successfully prevent all future lawsuits from the food industry.
options.B: They still suffer from significant delays and the loss of time and financial resources.
options.C: They are able to immediately implement all planned health regulations nationwide.
options.D: They receive financial compensation that covers the cost of public healthcare.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 B。根據文章第三段，即使政府贏得了官司，這些法律鬥爭往往持續多年，迫使官員花費時間與金錢在訴訟上，而非專注於公共衛生。選項 A 錯誤，因為文章未提及訴訟會停止；選項 C 錯誤，因為文章強調的是過程帶來的延遲；選項 D 錯誤，文章提到的是醫療費用支出，而非政府獲得賠償。

quiz.question: What can be inferred about the 'regulatory chill' mentioned in the fourth paragraph?

options.A: It is a deliberate strategy used by food companies to improve their public image.
options.B: It results from governments choosing to stop eating ultra-processed foods entirely.
options.C: It acts as a deterrent that makes governments hesitant to enact new health-related legislation.
options.D: It is a temporary condition that only affects countries with very small economies.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 C。根據第四段，『regulatory chill』是指政府因擔心昂貴且漫長的法律挑戰，而不敢通過類似的健康法案。這是一種因恐懼而產生的政策停滯。選項 A 錯誤，這是對抗手段而非形象工程；選項 B 錯誤，這是對政府的影響而非飲食習慣；選項 D 錯誤，文章並未限制其影響範圍僅限於小型經濟體。

quiz.question: In the fifth paragraph, what does the word 'rollout' mean in the context of new laws?

options.A: The physical printing and distribution of legal documents.
options.B: The process of officially introducing and implementing a new policy.
options.C: The act of canceling a law that was previously passed.
options.D: The public debate held before a law is officially drafted.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 B。在第五段中，『rollout』指的是新法律的推行或實施過程。選項 A 錯誤，這是對單詞的字面誤解；選項 C 錯誤，這與文章中提到的阻礙推行（slow down）相反；選項 D 錯誤，這是在法律正式實施前的階段，而非推行本身。

quiz.question: Which of the following best summarizes the central message of the article?

options.A: Food companies are working hard to educate the public about healthy eating habits.
options.B: Global obesity is primarily caused by a lack of exercise rather than food consumption.
options.C: Legal challenges from food companies are used as a strategic tool to delay health regulations, hindering public health efforts.
options.D: Governments have successfully eliminated all obstacles to passing laws against ultra-processed foods.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 C。全文的核心在於揭露大型食品公司如何利用法律手段來阻撓或延後各國政府推動的公共衛生政策，進而對全球肥胖防治造成負面影響。選項 A 與文章主旨相反；選項 B 文中未提及運動與肥胖的因果關係；選項 D 與文章內容矛盾，因為政府目前仍面臨巨大的法律壓力與挑戰。
